about.title: Norwalk Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Norwalk sits in the southeast corner of Los Angeles County, and a good share of its 107,140 residents earn a living on their feet, behind a wheel, or on a job site. When a workday ends in an injury, the first question is usually simple: who pays? In California, your employer's workers' compensation coverage normally answers that, regardless of who was at fault. It is meant to cover medical care and a portion of lost wages, and it is generally the only claim you can bring against the employer itself. Yet many Norwalk injuries involve someone outside your own company. Think of a delivery driver struck on Imperial Highway or Rosecrans Avenue, a subcontractor hurt by another crew's equipment, or a worker injured by a defective tool. Those situations can support a separate third-party claim with its own two-year filing window. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent attorney who can sort out which claims apply, at no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: We Explain the Two-Track System
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party such as a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker can open a separate claim. An attorney in our network can review whether both tracks apply to you.

items.title: Deadlines Are Taken Seriously
items.desc: California asks you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and third-party claims generally carry a two-year deadline. Connecting early gives an independent attorney room to protect both.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal, and You Deserve Backup
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from punishing you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. The attorneys we connect you with work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was hit while driving for work on Imperial Highway in Norwalk. Is that a workers' comp case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It may be both. Because you were on the job, workers' compensation typically applies regardless of fault. If another driver caused the crash, you may also have a separate third-party injury claim against that driver, and Norwalk recorded 413 injury collisions in 2025, so this overlap comes up more than people expect. An independent attorney can evaluate how the two claims interact.

items.question: Do I have to report my injury to my employer, and how quickly?
items.answer: Yes. California generally expects you to notify your employer within 30 days of a work injury, ideally in writing. Reporting late can complicate your workers' compensation benefits, and your employer is not allowed to retaliate against you for reporting.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm, and what does it cost?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is not a law firm and we do not give legal advice. We are a free service that connects injured people in Norwalk with an independent personal injury attorney. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, which means there is no fee unless there is a recovery.
